ordered_diagnoses: Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion with Neovascularization

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive retinal vascular proliferation with macular edema resolution
salient_findings: Macular edema resolution after intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Hyperreflective tissues proliferating on retinal vessels on OCTA
Dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography
key_facts: 76-year-old woman presented with macular edema
Treated with 2 intravitreal anti-VEGF injections
Macular edema completely resolved at 3 months
No recurrence of macular edema
OCTA findings showed hyperreflective tissues at 12 months
OCTA B-scan showed pyramid-shaped proliferations at 12 months
Hyperreflective tissues increased in size at 15 months
Angiogenic sprouts showed flow signals extending vertically at 15 months
Development observed in area of preexisting proliferation at 18 months
Enlarged horizontal structures along retina surface at 21 months
Fluorescein Angiography showed dendritic vascular-like structures at 21 months

shortlist.label: Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive retinal vascular proliferation and history of macular edema

shortlist.label: Coats Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Retinal vascular abnormalities and presence of hyperreflective tissues

shortlist.why_kept: History of macular edema and presence of neovascularization

shortlist.label: Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion with Neovascularization

raw.rationale: The patient's age and the progression of hyperreflective tissues and angiogenic sprouts on OCTA, along with the presence of dendritic vascular-like structures on Fluorescein Angiography, are consistent with the characteristics of proliferative diabetic retinopathy, which is known for its neovascularization and potential for vision-threatening complications.

rejected.label: Coats Disease
rejected.why: Typically affects younger males and does not usually present with the sequential development of neovascularization as seen in this case

rejected.label: Eales Disease
rejected.why: Characterized by retinal vasculitis and neovascularization, but the age and specific OCTA findings do not align closely with this diagnosis

rejected.label: Retinal Vein Occlusion with Neovascularization
rejected.why: The absence of a reported retinal vein occlusion and the specific pattern of neovascularization make this less likely

rejected.label: Branch Retinal Vein Occlusion with Neovascularization
rejected.why: Similar to retinal vein occlusion, there's no indication of a branch retinal vein occlusion in the provided information
